trail.candidate_family: iodomethane oxidative addition to rhodium(I) acetylacetonato carbonyl triphenylphosphine

barrier_quantity.type: PW91/TZP/COSMO(methanol) calculated Gibbs free energy of activation at 298.15 K for the favored linear/back associative SN2 oxidative-addition transition state, relative to the separated computational reactants
barrier_quantity.method_provenance: PW91 functional, TZP basis, COSMO solvent model with methanol dielectric; reactants taken as energy zero
typing_firewall: not an experimental activation free energy
not a raw observed rate constant
24 kJ/mol electronic activation energy and 27 kJ/mol activation enthalpy are retained as distinct quantities and are not silently substituted for 71 kJ/mol

observed_comparator.event: formation of the first Rh(III)-alkyl oxidative-addition product under pseudo-first-order CH3I excess
observed_comparator.raw_kinetic_support: temperature- and CH3I-concentration-dependent pseudo-first-order k_obs values are publicly reproduced for the PPh3 complex in dichloromethane

condition_mismatch.reason: The 71 kJ/mol theoretical free-energy barrier was calculated with COSMO methanol, while the independent 2010 raw kinetic comparator was measured in dichloromethane. The solvent dependence of an associative charged/polar transition state cannot be assumed negligible or repaired by ad hoc residual matching.

trail.independence_note: The 2011 computational study explicitly compares its 71 kJ/mol result with known experimental activation quantities. No same-target parameter fitting is established by the sources audited here, but independence from target-informed method/transition-state selection is not presumed. The computational method lineage must be reconstructed before promotion.
trail.network_note: Subsequent carbonyl insertion/deinsertion and alkyl/acyl isomerization belong to later steps and are not substituted for the first oxidative-addition event comparator.
next_gate: Locate a prospectively independent theoretical barrier/free-energy calculation for the same elementary oxidative-addition event in dichloromethane at approximately 298 K with explicit standard-state treatment, or locate independent raw kinetics in methanol at approximately 298 K matching the existing PW91/TZP/COSMO barrier.

Reconstruct the PW91/TZP method-selection lineage and establish whether choices were fixed independently of the selected kinetic target; if target-informed tuning or model selection is found, quarantine that calculation from validation.
Do not use the experimental 82 kJ/mol Eyring free energy or 38.8 kJ/mol activation enthalpy as an independent barrier because they are derived from the same kinetics being validated.
